title: O'Neil Spencer, John Kirby's drummer
summary: Jones remembers O'Neil Spencer's drinking, knitting and playing with John Kirby.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Speaking about taking a job, you always remember Mr. O'Neil Spencer -
I was going to ask you about him next, a great drummer with the John Kirby band.

With John Kirby. But before he was with the Blue Mills Rhythm Boys... He quit drinking and he joined George, uh, John Kirby. He hadn't had a drink in 6 months and I went in Joe Hawkes place and I said, "I want to buy him a beer. This is his birthday; he hasn't had a drink in 6 months." And he took a drink and then he took up knitting, which was a very therapeutic thing. You know, John was with Maxine Sullivan and they went out and did tours and what have you. John Kirby had the most classical, he had a class band. Now O'Neil Spencer, me and Sidney would say, "All right. Give him a shorty." He had a good job and me and Sidney would go down around on the job and say, "He's not here?" He was making $20 a night, so we had $2 and we'd put him in a booth and he'd be drunk and me and Sidney would collect $18 and come back in the bar and he's still laying up in the booth. But he was a beautiful man and a beautiful player. I didn't know that he could play tymos and vibraphones and chimes, but I found out he could.
